english: And thus we can say that consciousness could never be something—no matter which way you look at it—that could exist through some nature of its own. Such a thing would be similar to the strand of hair that those who have cataracts think they see—something like that. If you say that something exists only because it has an erroneous factor, then for the very same reason we'd have to say that if something lacked an erroneous factor, then it couldn't exist at all. At least, that's the way it seems to me.
